title: Across seven open-weight AI model families, does adding automated clinical rules help every model?
summary: Seven open-weight AI models (Google Gemma 4 12B, Alibaba Qwen 3 14B, Mistral NeMo 12B, Meta Llama 3.1 8B, IBM Granite 3.3 8B, Liquid LFM2 8B, and medical-tuned MedGemma 4B) answered eight clinical questions across five patients. Each model was tested twice — once reading the condensed patient chart on its own, and once with our automated clinical rule checks attached — and graded by two independent AI judges.
takeaway: Attaching automated clinical rule checks improved every general AI model by 6 to 21 points. Google's Gemma 4 12B with clinical rules led overall (91.0/100, zero unsafe answers), followed by Alibaba's Qwen 3 14B (83.1/100, zero unsafe answers). Reading the chart alone, even strong models frequently missed duplicate brand-name vs. generic prescriptions (such as taking Plavix and clopidogrel together) or multi-step vaccine timing rules.
